implementation_notes: C++ is the language where the classic form is most justified: virtual functions (cppreference) give exactly the AbstractFactory/ConcreteFactory pair, and clients hold WidgetFactory& plus abstract product references. Return std::unique_ptr<Product> from the factory methods so ownership is explicit and the factory never retains the product; use std::function fields when the family is assembled from configuration or needs per-field test stubs, and a template policy when the family is a compile-time decision and zero abstraction cost is required. Keep the factory interface narrow; a new product kind changes every override set.
pitfalls: Missing virtual destructor on the factory base: deleting through the base pointer is undefined behaviour.
Raw owning pointers returned from factory methods break encapsulation of ownership; use std::unique_ptr (C++11) or std::shared_ptr when sharing is genuinely required.
Template policies look free but make the family compile-time-fixed: misapplying them produces code that cannot be reconfigured without recompilation.
Returning std::unique_ptr from a factory but storing it in a raw pointer discards ownership semantics; always use smart pointers in client signatures.

variants.name: Struct of std::function creators (type-erased factory)
variants.implementation_notes: Replace the class hierarchy with a struct of std::function members: each field is a creator for one product kind and any lambda, free function or functor can fill it, so the family is assembled at runtime from configuration or plugin code. Individual fields can be swapped independently, which makes test stubs a one-line lambda instead of a derived mock class; the price is std::function's type-erasure overhead and no compile-time check that all fields were set. This variant is particularly useful when the family is selected from a config file or plugin registry at startup.
pitfalls: An empty std::function member throws std::bad_function_call at creation time - validate the struct before use.
Type erasure costs an indirect call and a possible allocation per creation; in hot paths prefer the virtual or template variant.
Because fields are public, two creators from different families can be mixed accidentally, losing the consistency guarantee.

std::function requires a CopyConstructible callable, so a lambda that captures std::unique_ptr cannot be stored in it at all; use std::move_only_function (C++23) or capture shared/value state when move-only ownership is required.
